{"actor_id":"EO:13470","char_end":1122,"char_start":609,"confidence":"medium","effective_class":"unknown","effective_date":null,"effective_wording":[{"char_end":6400,"char_start":6318,"text":"The Director will lead a unified, \ncoordinated, and effective intelligence effort."},{"char_end":12214,"char_start":7790,"text":"(b) In addition to fulfilling the obligations and responsibilities prescribed \nby the Act, the Director: \n(1) Shall establish objectives, priorities, and guidance for the Intelligence \nCommunity to ensure timely and effective collection, processing, analysis, \nVerDate Aug<31>2005 17:10 Aug 01, 2008 Jkt 214001 PO 00000 Frm 00004 Fmt 4705 Sfmt 4790 E:\\FR\\FM\\04AUE0.SGM 04AUE0pwalker on PROD1PC71 with NOTICES3\n=== PDF page 3 of 18 ===\n45327 Federal Register / Vol. 73, No. 150 / Monday, August 4, 2008 / Presidential Documents \nand dissemination of intelligence, of whatever nature and from whatever \nsource derived; \n(2) May designate, in consultation with affected heads of departments \nor Intelligence Community elements, one or more Intelligence Community \nelements to develop and to maintain services of common concern on \nbehalf of the Intelligence Community if the Director determines such \nservices can be more efficiently or effectively accomplished in a consoli-\ndated manner; \n(3) Shall oversee and provide advice to the President and the NSC with \nrespect to all ongoing and proposed covert action programs; \n(4) In regard to the establishment and conduct of intelligence arrangements \nand agreements with foreign governments and international organizations: \n(A) May enter into intelligence and counterintelligence arrangements \nand agreements with foreign governments and international organiza-\ntions; \n(B) Shall formulate policies concerning intelligence and counterintel-\nligence arrangements and agreements with foreign governments and \ninternational organizations; and \n(C) Shall align and synchronize intelligence and counterintelligence \nforeign relationships among the elements of the Intelligence Commu-\nnity to further United States national security, policy, and intelligence \nobjectives; \n(5) Shall participate in the development of procedures approved by the \nAttorney General governing criminal drug intelligence activities abroad \nto ensure that these activities are consistent with foreign intelligence pro-\ngrams; \n(6) Shall establish common security and access standards for managing \nand handling intelligence systems, information, and products, with special \nemphasis on facilitating: \n(A) The fullest and most prompt access to and dissemination of infor-\nmation and intelligence practicable, assigning the highest priority to \ndetecting, preventing, preempting, and disrupting terrorist threats and \nactivities against the United States, its interests, and allies; and \n(B) The establishment of standards for an interoperable information \nsharing enterprise that facilitates the sharing of intelligence informa-\ntion among elements of the Intelligence Community; \n(7) Shall ensure that appropriate departments and agencies have access \nto intelligence and receive the support needed to perform independent \nanalysis; \n(8) Shall protect, and ensure that programs are developed to protect, \nintelligence sources, methods, and activities from unauthorized disclosure; \n(9) Shall, after consultation with the heads of affected departments and \nagencies, establish guidelines for Intelligence Community elements for: \n(A) Classification and declassification of all intelligence and intel-\nligence-related information classified under the authority of the Direc-\ntor or the authority of the head of a department or Intelligence Com-\nmunity element; and \n(B) Access to and dissemination of all intelligence and intelligence- \nrelated information, both in its final form and in the form when ini-\ntially gathered, to include intelligence originally classified by the head \nof a department or Intelligence Community element, except that ac-\ncess to and dissemination of information concerning United States \npersons shall be governed by procedures developed in accordance \nwith Part 2 of this order; \n(10) May, only with respect to Intelligence Community elements, and \nafter consultation with thehead of the originating Intelligence Community \nelement or the head of the originating department, declassify, or direct \nthe declassification of, information or intelligence relating to intelligence \nVerDate Aug<31>2005 17:10 Aug 01, 2008 Jkt 214001 PO 00000 Frm 00005 Fmt 4705 Sfmt 4790 E:\\FR\\FM\\04AUE0.SGM 04AUE0pwalker on PROD1PC71 with NOTICES3\n=== PDF page 4 of 18 ===\n45328 Federal Register / Vol. 73, No. 150 / Monday, August 4, 2008 / Presidential Documents \nsources, methods, and activities."},{"char_end":20796,"char_start":19755,"text":"Directives issued and actions taken by the Director in the exercise \nof the Director ’s authorities and responsibilities to integrate, coordinate, \nand make the Intelligence Community more effective in providing intelligence \nrelated to national security shall be implemented by the elements of the \nIntelligence Community, provided that any department head whose depart-\nment contains an element of the Intelligence Community and who believes \nthat a directive or action of the Director violates the requirements of section \n1018 of the IRTPA or this subsection shall bring the issue to the attention \nVerDate Aug<31>2005 17:10 Aug 01, 2008 Jkt 214001 PO 00000 Frm 00007 Fmt 4705 Sfmt 4790 E:\\FR\\FM\\04AUE0.SGM 04AUE0pwalker on PROD1PC71 with NOTICES3\n=== PDF page 6 of 18 ===\n45330 Federal Register / Vol. 73, No. 150 / Monday, August 4, 2008 / Presidential Documents \nof the Director, the NSC, or the President for resolution in a manner that \nrespects and does not abrogate the statutory responsibilities of the heads \nof the departments."},{"char_end":37987,"char_start":37441,"text":"The Director of the National \nSecurity Agency shall: \n(1) Collect (including through clandestine means), process, analyze, \nproduce, and disseminate signals intelligence information and data for \nforeign intelligence and counterintelligence purposes to support national \nand departmental missions; \n(2) Establish and operate an effective unified organization for signals intel-\nligence activities, except for the delegation of operational control over \ncertain operations that are conducted through other elements of the Intel-\nligence Community."}],"exceptions_text":[],"filing_date":null,"id":"ACT:EO:12333>EO:13470#609-amend","names_target":true,"notes":"Machine lead only; no legal ending or revival asserted. - **ACT:EO:12333>EO:13470@0ee28878ea3ee65a**; S9341949dfc7e0482b02724dd; {"actor_id":"EO:13470","char_end":1611,"char_start":1123,"confidence":"medium","effective_class":"unknown","effective_date":null,"effective_wording":[{"char_end":6400,"char_start":6318,"text":"The Director will lead a unified, \ncoordinated, and effective intelligence effort."},{"char_end":12214,"char_start":7790,"text":"(b) In addition to fulfilling the obligations and responsibilities prescribed \nby the Act, the Director: \n(1) Shall establish objectives, priorities, and guidance for the Intelligence \nCommunity to ensure timely and effective collection, processing, analysis, \nVerDate Aug<31>2005 17:10 Aug 01, 2008 Jkt 214001 PO 00000 Frm 00004 Fmt 4705 Sfmt 4790 E:\\FR\\FM\\04AUE0.SGM 04AUE0pwalker on PROD1PC71 with NOTICES3\n=== PDF page 3 of 18 ===\n45327 Federal Register / Vol. 73, No. 150 / Monday, August 4, 2008 / Presidential Documents \nand dissemination of intelligence, of whatever nature and from whatever \nsource derived; \n(2) May designate, in consultation with affected heads of departments \nor Intelligence Community elements, one or more Intelligence Community \nelements to develop and to maintain services of common concern on \nbehalf of the Intelligence Community if the Director determines such \nservices can be more efficiently or effectively accomplished in a consoli-\ndated manner; \n(3) Shall oversee and provide advice to the President and the NSC with \nrespect to all ongoing and proposed covert action programs; \n(4) In regard to the establishment and conduct of intelligence arrangements \nand agreements with foreign governments and international organizations: \n(A) May enter into intelligence and counterintelligence arrangements \nand agreements with foreign governments and international organiza-\ntions; \n(B) Shall formulate policies concerning intelligence and counterintel-\nligence arrangements and agreements with foreign governments and \ninternational organizations; and \n(C) Shall align and synchronize intelligence and counterintelligence \nforeign relationships among the elements of the Intelligence Commu-\nnity to further United States national security, policy, and intelligence \nobjectives; \n(5) Shall participate in the development of procedures approved by the \nAttorney General governing criminal drug intelligence activities abroad \nto ensure that these activities are consistent with foreign intelligence pro-\ngrams; \n(6) Shall establish common security and access standards for managing \nand handling intelligence systems, information, and products, with special \nemphasis on facilitating: \n(A) The fullest and most prompt access to and dissemination of infor-\nmation and intelligence practicable, assigning the highest priority to \ndetecting, preventing, preempting, and disrupting terrorist threats and \nactivities against the United States, its interests, and allies; and \n(B) The establishment of standards for an interoperable information \nsharing enterprise that facilitates the sharing of intelligence informa-\ntion among elements of the Intelligence Community; \n(7) Shall ensure that appropriate departments and agencies have access \nto intelligence and receive the support needed to perform independent \nanalysis; \n(8) Shall protect, and ensure that programs are developed to protect, \nintelligence sources, methods, and activities from unauthorized disclosure; \n(9) Shall, after consultation with the heads of affected departments and \nagencies, establish guidelines for Intelligence Community elements for: \n(A) Classification and declassification of all intelligence and intel-\nligence-related information classified under the authority of the Direc-\ntor or the authority of the head of a department or Intelligence Com-\nmunity element; and \n(B) Access to and dissemination of all intelligence and intelligence- \nrelated information, both in its final form and in the form when ini-\ntially gathered, to include intelligence originally classified by the head \nof a department or Intelligence Community element, except that ac-\ncess to and dissemination of information concerning United States \npersons shall be governed by procedures developed in accordance \nwith Part 2 of this order; \n(10) May, only with respect to Intelligence Community elements, and \nafter consultation with thehead of the originating Intelligence Community \nelement or the head of the originating department, declassify, or direct \nthe declassification of, information or intelligence relating to intelligence \nVerDate Aug<31>2005 17:10 Aug 01, 2008 Jkt 214001 PO 00000 Frm 00005 Fmt 4705 Sfmt 4790 E:\\FR\\FM\\04AUE0.SGM 04AUE0pwalker on PROD1PC71 with NOTICES3\n=== PDF page 4 of 18 ===\n45328 Federal Register / Vol. 73, No. 150 / Monday, August 4, 2008 / Presidential Documents \nsources, methods, and activities."},{"char_end":20796,"char_start":19755,"text":"Directives issued and actions taken by the Director in the exercise \nof the Director ’s authorities and responsibilities to integrate, coordinate, \nand make the Intelligence Community more effective in providing intelligence \nrelated to national security shall be implemented by the elements of the \nIntelligence Community, provided that any department head whose depart-\nment contains an element of the Intelligence Community and who believes \nthat a directive or action of the Director violates the requirements of section \n1018 of the IRTPA or this subsection shall bring the issue to the attention \nVerDate Aug<31>2005 17:10 Aug 01, 2008 Jkt 214001 PO 00000 Frm 00007 Fmt 4705 Sfmt 4790 E:\\FR\\FM\\04AUE0.SGM 04AUE0pwalker on PROD1PC71 with NOTICES3\n=== PDF page 6 of 18 ===\n45330 Federal Register / Vol. 73, No. 150 / Monday, August 4, 2008 / Presidential Documents \nof the Director, the NSC, or the President for resolution in a manner that \nrespects and does not abrogate the statutory responsibilities of the heads \nof the departments."},{"char_end":37987,"char_start":37441,"text":"The Director of the National \nSecurity Agency shall: \n(1) Collect (including through clandestine means), process, analyze, \nproduce, and disseminate signals intelligence information and data for \nforeign intelligence and counterintelligence purposes to support national \nand departmental missions; \n(2) Establish and operate an effective unified organization for signals intel-\nligence activities, except for the delegation of operational control over \ncertain operations that are conducted through other elements of the Intel-\nligence Community."}],"exceptions_text":[],"filing_date":null,"id":"ACT:EO:12333>EO:13470@0ee28878ea3ee65a","names_target":true,"notes":"Machine lead only; no legal ending or revival asserted. consultation with affected heads of departments \nor Intelligence Community elements, one or more Intelligence Community \nelements to develop and to maintain services of common concern on \nbehalf of the Intelligence Community if the Director determines such \nservices can be more efficiently or effectively accomplished in a consoli-\ndated manner; \n(3) Shall oversee and provide advice to the President and the NSC with \nrespect to all ongoing and proposed covert action programs; \n(4) In regard to the establishment and conduct of intelligence arrangements \nand agreements with foreign governments and international organizations: \n(A) May enter into intelligence and counterintelligence arrangements \nand agreements with foreign governments and international organiza-\ntions; \n(B) Shall formulate policies concerning intelligence and counterintel-\nligence arrangements and agreements with foreign governments and \ninternational organizations; and \n(C) Shall align and synchronize intelligence and counterintelligence \nforeign relationships among the elements of the Intelligence Commu-\nnity to further United States national security, policy, and intelligence \nobjectives; \n(5) Shall participate in the development of procedures approved by the \nAttorney General governing criminal drug intelligence activities abroad \nto ensure that these activities are consistent with foreign intelligence pro-\ngrams; \n(6) Shall establish common security and access standards for managing \nand handling intelligence systems, information, and products, with special \nemphasis on facilitating: \n(A) The fullest and most prompt access to and dissemination of infor-\nmation and intelligence practicable, assigning the highest priority to \ndetecting, preventing, preempting, and disrupting terrorist threats and \nactivities against the United States, its interests, and allies; and \n(B) The establishment of standards for an interoperable information \nsharing enterprise that facilitates the sharing of intelligence informa-\ntion among elements of the Intelligence Community; \n(7) Shall ensure that appropriate departments and agencies have access \nto intelligence and receive the support needed to perform independent \nanalysis; \n(8) Shall protect, and ensure that programs are developed to protect, \nintelligence sources, methods, and activities from unauthorized disclosure; \n(9) Shall, after consultation with the heads of affected departments and \nagencies, establish guidelines for Intelligence Community elements for: \n(A) Classification and declassification of all intelligence and intel-\nligence-related information classified under the authority of the Direc-\ntor or the authority of the head of a department or Intelligence Com-\nmunity element; and \n(B) Access to and dissemination of all intelligence and intelligence- \nrelated information, both in its final form and in the form when ini-\ntially gathered, to include intelligence originally classified by the head \nof a department or Intelligence Community element, except that ac-\ncess to and dissemination of information concerning United States \npersons shall be governed by procedures developed in accordance \nwith Part 2 of this order; \n(10) May, only with respect to Intelligence Community elements, and \nafter consultation with thehead of the originating Intelligence Community \nelement or the head of the originating department, declassify, or direct \nthe declassification of, information or intelligence relating to intelligence \nVerDate Aug<31>2005 17:10 Aug 01, 2008 Jkt 214001 PO 00000 Frm 00005 Fmt 4705 Sfmt 4790 E:\\FR\\FM\\04AUE0.SGM 04AUE0pwalker on PROD1PC71 with NOTICES3\n=== PDF page 4 of 18 ===\n45328 Federal Register / Vol. 73, No. 150 / Monday, August 4, 2008 / Presidential Documents \nsources, methods, and activities."},{"char_end":20187,"char_start":19146,"text":"Directives issued and actions taken by the Director in security shall be implemented by the elements of the \nIntelligence Community, provided that any department head whose depart-\nment contains an element of the Intelligence Community and who believes \nthat a directive or action of the Director violates the requirements of section \n1018 of the IRTPA or this subsection shall bring the issue to the attention \nVerDate Aug<31>2005 17:10 Aug 01, 2008 Jkt 214001 PO 00000 Frm 00007 Fmt 4705 Sfmt 4790 E:\\FR\\FM\\04AUE0.SGM 04AUE0pwalker on PROD1PC71 with NOTICES3\n=== PDF page 6 of 18 ===\n45330 Federal Register / Vol. 73, No. 150 / Monday, August departments."},{"char_end":37378,"char_start":36832,"text":"The Director of the National \nSecurity Agency shall: \n(1) Collect (including through clandestine means), process, analyze, \nproduce, and disseminate signals intelligence information and data for \nforeign intelligence and counterintelligence purposes to support national \nand departmental missions; \n(2) Establish and operate an effective unified organization for signals intel-\nligence activities, except for the delegation of operational control over \ncertain operations that are conducted through other elements of the Intel-\nligence Community."}],"exceptions_text":[],"filing_date":null,"id":"ACT:EO:12333>EO:13470@283210034d79b123","names_target":true,"notes":"Machine lead only; no legal ending or revival asserted. - **ACT:EO:12333>EO:13470@39be29b605300aeb**; S96ea439fd98180fd04b7e16f; {"actor_id":"EO:13470","char_end":1001,"char_start":859,"confidence":"medium","effective_class":"unknown","effective_date":null,"effective_wording":[{"char_end":5321,"char_start":5240,"text":"The Director will lead a unified, coordinated, and effective intelligence effort."},{"char_end":7040,"char_start":6800,"text":"(1) Shall establish objectives, priorities, and guidance for the Intelligence Community to ensure timely and effective collection, processing, analysis, and dissemination of intelligence, of whatever nature and from whatever source derived;"},{"char_end":18492,"char_start":17730,"text":"Directives issued and actions taken by the Director in the exercise of the Director's authorities and responsibilities to integrate, coordinate, and make the Intelligence Community more effective in providing intelligence related to national security shall be implemented by the elements of the Intelligence Community, provided that any department head whose department contains an element of the Intelligence Community and who believes that a directive or action of the Director violates the requirements of section 1018 of the IRTPA or this subsection shall bring the issue to the attention of the Director, the NSC, or the President for resolution in a manner that respects and does not abrogate the statutory responsibilities of the heads of the departments."},{"char_end":34413,"char_start":34171,"text":"(2) Establish and operate an effective unified organization for signals intelligence activities, except for the delegation of operational control over certain operations that are conducted through other elements of the Intelligence Community."}],"exceptions_text":[],"filing_date":null,"id":"ACT:EO:12333>EO:13470@39be29b605300aeb","names_target":true,"notes":"Machine lead only; no legal ending or revival asserted. Effective wording is ambiguous, section-specific, or has no determinable date. {"actor_id":"EO:13470","char_end":1884,"char_start":1621,"confidence":"medium","effective_class":"unknown","effective_date":null,"effective_wording":[{"char_end":6400,"char_start":6318,"text":"The Director will lead a unified, \ncoordinated, and effective intelligence effort."},{"char_end":12214,"char_start":7790,"text":"(b) In addition to fulfilling the obligations and responsibilities prescribed \nby the Act, the Director: \n(1) Shall establish objectives, priorities, and guidance for the Intelligence \nCommunity to ensure timely and effective collection, processing, analysis, \nVerDate Aug<31>2005 17:10 Aug 01, 2008 Jkt 214001 PO 00000 Frm 00004 Fmt 4705 Sfmt 4790 E:\\FR\\FM\\04AUE0.SGM 04AUE0pwalker on PROD1PC71 with NOTICES3\n=== PDF page 3 of 18 ===\n45327 Federal Register / Vol. 73, No. 150 / Monday, August 4, 2008 / Presidential Documents \nand dissemination of intelligence, of whatever nature and from whatever \nsource derived; \n(2) May designate, in consultation with affected heads of departments \nor Intelligence Community elements, one or more Intelligence Community \nelements to develop and to maintain services of common concern on \nbehalf of the Intelligence Community if the Director determines such \nservices can be more efficiently or effectively accomplished in a consoli-\ndated manner; \n(3) Shall oversee and provide advice to the President and the NSC with \nrespect to all ongoing and proposed covert action programs; \n(4) In regard to the establishment and conduct of intelligence arrangements \nand agreements with foreign governments and international organizations: \n(A) May enter into intelligence and counterintelligence arrangements \nand agreements with foreign governments and international organiza-\ntions; \n(B) Shall formulate policies concerning intelligence and counterintel-\nligence arrangements and agreements with foreign governments and \ninternational organizations; and \n(C) Shall align and synchronize intelligence and counterintelligence \nforeign relationships among the elements of the Intelligence Commu-\nnity to further United States national security, policy, and intelligence \nobjectives; \n(5) Shall participate in the development of procedures approved by the \nAttorney General governing criminal drug intelligence activities abroad \nto ensure that these activities are consistent with foreign intelligence pro-\ngrams; \n(6) Shall establish common security and access standards for managing \nand handling intelligence systems, information, and products, with special \nemphasis on facilitating: \n(A) The fullest and most prompt access to and dissemination of infor-\nmation and intelligence practicable, assigning the highest priority to \ndetecting, preventing, preempting, and disrupting terrorist threats and \nactivities against the United States, its interests, and allies; and \n(B) The establishment of standards for an interoperable information \nsharing enterprise that facilitates the sharing of intelligence informa-\ntion among elements of the Intelligence Community; \n(7) Shall ensure that appropriate departments and agencies have access \nto intelligence and receive the support needed to perform independent \nanalysis; \n(8) Shall protect, and ensure that programs are developed to protect, \nintelligence sources, methods, and activities from unauthorized disclosure; \n(9) Shall, after consultation with the heads of affected departments and \nagencies, establish guidelines for Intelligence Community elements for: \n(A) Classification and declassification of all intelligence and intel-\nligence-related information classified under the authority of the Direc-\ntor or the authority of the head of a department or Intelligence Com-\nmunity element; and \n(B) Access to and dissemination of all intelligence and intelligence- \nrelated information, both in its final form and in the form when ini-\ntially gathered, to include intelligence originally classified by the head \nof a department or Intelligence Community element, except that ac-\ncess to and dissemination of information concerning United States \npersons shall be governed by procedures developed in accordance \nwith Part 2 of this order; \n(10) May, only with respect to Intelligence Community elements, and \nafter consultation with thehead of the originating Intelligence Community \nelement or the head of the originating department, declassify, or direct \nthe declassification of, information or intelligence relating to intelligence \nVerDate consultation with affected heads of departments \nor Intelligence Community elements, one or more Intelligence Community \nelements to develop and to maintain services of common concern on \nbehalf of the Intelligence Community if the Director determines such \nservices can be more efficiently or effectively accomplished in a consoli-\ndated manner; \n(3) Shall oversee and provide advice to the President and the NSC with \nrespect to all ongoing and proposed covert action programs; \n(4) In regard to the establishment and conduct of intelligence arrangements \nand agreements with foreign governments and international organizations: \n(A) May enter into intelligence and counterintelligence arrangements \nand agreements with foreign governments and international organiza-\ntions; \n(B) Shall formulate policies concerning intelligence and counterintel-\nligence arrangements and agreements with foreign governments and \ninternational organizations; and \n(C) Shall align and synchronize intelligence and counterintelligence \nforeign relationships among the elements of the Intelligence Commu-\nnity to further United States national security, policy, and intelligence \nobjectives; \n(5) Shall participate in the development of procedures approved by the \nAttorney General governing criminal drug intelligence activities abroad \nto ensure that these activities are consistent with foreign intelligence pro-\ngrams; \n(6) Shall establish common security and access standards for managing \nand handling intelligence systems, information, and products, with special \nemphasis on facilitating: \n(A) The fullest and most prompt access to and dissemination of infor-\nmation and intelligence practicable, assigning the highest priority to \ndetecting, preventing, preempting, and disrupting terrorist threats and \nactivities against the United States, its interests, and allies; and \n(B) The establishment of standards for an interoperable information \nsharing enterprise that facilitates the sharing of intelligence informa-\ntion among elements of the Intelligence Community; \n(7) Shall ensure that appropriate departments and agencies have access \nto intelligence and receive the support needed to perform independent \nanalysis; \n(8) Shall protect, and ensure that programs are developed to protect, \nintelligence sources, methods, and activities from unauthorized disclosure; \n(9) Shall, after consultation with the heads of affected departments and \nagencies, establish guidelines for Intelligence Community elements for: \n(A) Classification and declassification of all intelligence and intel-\nligence-related information classified under the authority of the Direc-\ntor or the authority of the head of a department or Intelligence Com-\nmunity element; and \n(B) Access to and dissemination of all intelligence and intelligence- \nrelated information, both in its final form and in the form when ini-\ntially gathered, to include intelligence originally classified by the head \nof a department or Intelligence Community element, except that ac-\ncess to and dissemination of information concerning United States \npersons shall be governed by procedures developed in accordance \nwith Part 2 of this order; \n(10) May, only with respect to Intelligence Community elements, and \nafter consultation with thehead of the originating Intelligence Community \nelement or the head of the originating department, declassify, or direct \nthe declassification of, information or intelligence relating to intelligence \nVerDate Aug<31>2005 17:10 Aug 01, 2008 Jkt 214001 PO 00000 Frm 00005 Fmt 4705 Sfmt 4790 E:\\FR\\FM\\04AUE0.SGM 04AUE0pwalker on PROD1PC71 with NOTICES3\n=== PDF page 4 of 18 ===\n45328 Federal Register / Vol. effective unified organization for signals intel-\nligence activities, except for the delegation of operational control over \ncertain operations that are conducted through other elements of the Shall formulate policies concerning intelligence and counterintel-\nligence arrangements and agreements with foreign governments and \ninternational organizations; and \n(C) Shall align and synchronize intelligence and counterintelligence \nforeign relationships among the elements of the Intelligence Commu-\nnity to further United States national security, policy, and intelligence \nobjectives; \n(5) Shall participate in the development of procedures approved by the \nAttorney General governing criminal drug intelligence activities abroad \nto ensure that these activities are consistent with foreign intelligence pro-\ngrams; \n(6) Shall establish common security and access standards for managing \nand handling intelligence systems, information, and products, with special \nemphasis on facilitating: \n(A) The fullest and most prompt access to and dissemination of infor-\nmation and intelligence practicable, assigning the highest priority to \ndetecting, preventing, preempting, and disrupting terrorist threats and \nactivities against the United States, its interests, and allies; and \n(B) The establishment of standards for an interoperable information \nsharing enterprise that facilitates the sharing of intelligence informa-\ntion among elements of the Intelligence Community; \n(7) Shall ensure that appropriate departments and agencies have access \nto intelligence and receive the support needed to perform independent \nanalysis; \n(8) Shall protect, and ensure that programs are developed to protect, \nintelligence sources, methods, and activities from unauthorized disclosure; \n(9) Shall, after consultation with the heads of affected departments and \nagencies, establish guidelines for Intelligence Community elements for: \n(A) Classification be governed by procedures developed in accordance \nwith Part 2 of this order; \n(10) May, only with respect to Intelligence Community elements, and \nafter consultation with thehead of the \n(b) referring to the Steering Committee for resolution any unresolved issues \ndelaying the Executive Agent’s timely development and issuance of technical \npolicies and standards; \n(c) reporting at least annually to the Steering Committee on the work \nof CNSS, including recommendations for any changes needed to improve \nthe timeliness and effectiveness of that work; - **ACT:EO:12333>EO:13764**; S40d5b68f9666dd4854f4e4c0; {"actor_id":"EO:13764","char_end":54089,"char_start":53395,"confidence":"medium","effective_class":"unknown","effective_date":null,"effective_wording":[{"char_end":12781,"char_start":11378,"text":"(a) Executive branch vetting policies and procedures \nrelating to suitability, contractor or Federal employee fitness, eligibility to \nhold a sensitive position, authorization to be issued a Federal credential \nfor access to federally controlled facilities and information systems, and \nVerDate Sep<11>2014 21:05 Jan 19, 2017 Jkt 241001 PO 00000 Frm 00005 Fmt 4705 Sfmt 4790 E:\\FR\\FM\\23JAE0.SGM 23JAE0asabaliauskas on DSK3SPTVN1PROD with E0\n=== PDF page 4 of 15 ===\n8118 Federal Register / Vol. 82, No. 13 / Monday, January 23, 2017 / Presidential Documents \neligibility for access to classified information shall be aligned using consistent \nstandards to the extent possible, shall provide for reciprocal recognition, \nand shall ensure cost-effective, timely, and efficient protection of the national \ninterest, while providing fair treatment to those upon whom the Federal \nGovernment relies to conduct our Nation’s business and protect national \nsecurity. \n‘‘(b) The Government’s tools, systems, and processes for conducting these \nbackground investigations and managing sensitive investigative information \nshould keep pace with technological advancements, regularly integrating \ncurrent best practices to better anticipate, detect, and counter malicious \nactivities, and threats posed by external or internal actors who may seek \nto do harm to the Government’s personnel, property, and information."},{"char_end":13478,"char_start":12783,"text":"To help fulfill these responsibilities, there shall be a primary executive \nbranch investigative service provider whose mission is to provide effective, \nefficient, and secure background investigations for the Federal Government. \n‘‘(c) Executive branch vetting policies and procedures shall be sustained \nby an enhanced risk-management approach that facilitates early detection \nof issues by an informed, aware, and responsible Federal workforce; results \nin quality decisions enabled by improved vetting capabilities; and advances \nGovernment-wide capabilities through enterprise approaches. \n‘‘(d) The appointment or retention of each covered individual shall be \nsubject to an investigation."},{"char_end":23242,"char_start":19592,"text":"It relies on re-\nsearch to generate data-driven decisions and uses outcome-based measure-\nments to adjust policy and operations. \n‘‘(f) ‘Continuous vetting’ means reviewing the background of a covered \nindividual at any time to determine whether that individual continues \nto meet applicable requirements.’’ \n(i) Redesignated section 1.3(h) of Executive Order 13467 is revised to \nread as follows: \n‘‘(h) ‘Covered individual’ means a person who performs, or who seeks \nto perform, work for or on behalf of the executive branch (e.g., Federal \nemployee, military member, or contractor), or otherwise interacts with \nVerDate Sep<11>2014 21:05 Jan 19, 2017 Jkt 241001 PO 00000 Frm 00007 Fmt 4705 Sfmt 4790 E:\\FR\\FM\\23JAE0.SGM 23JAE0asabaliauskas on DSK3SPTVN1PROD with E0\n=== PDF page 6 of 15 ===\n8120 Federal Register / Vol. 82, No. 13 / Monday, January 23, 2017 / Presidential Documents \nthe executive branch such that the individual must undergo vetting, but \ndoes not include: \n‘‘(i) the President or (except to the extent otherwise directed by the \nPresident) employees of the President under section 105 or 107 of title \n3, United States Code; \n‘‘(ii) the Vice President or (except to the extent otherwise directed \nby the Vice President) employees of the Vice President under section \n106 of title 3, United States Code, or annual legislative branch appropria-\ntions acts; or \n‘‘(iii) with respect to background investigations only, duly elected or \nappointed governor of a State or territory, or an official who has succeeded \nto that office under applicable law in accordance with Executive Order \n13549 of August 18, 2010, and its implementing directive.’’ \n(j) New sections 1.3(k) and 1.3(l) are added to Executive Order 13467 \nto read as follows: \n‘‘(k) ‘Fitness’ means the level of character and conduct determined nec-\nessary for an individual to perform work for or on behalf of a Federal \nagency as an employee in the excepted service (other than a position \nsubject to suitability), or as a ‘contractor employee’ or a ‘nonappropriated \nfund employee’ as those terms are defined in Executive Order 13488 \nof January 16, 2009, as amended. \n‘‘(l) ‘Investigation’ means the collection and analysis of pertinent facts \nand data to support a determination of whether a covered individual \nis, and continues to be: \n‘‘(i) eligible for access to classified information; \n‘‘(ii) eligible to hold a sensitive position; \n‘‘(iii) suitable or fit for Federal employment; \n‘‘(iv) fit to perform work for or on behalf of the Federal Government \nas a contractor or nonappropriated fund employee; or \n‘‘(v) authorized to be issued a Federal credential.’’ \n(k) Redesignated section 1.3(n) of Executive Order 13467 is revised to \nread as follows: \n‘‘(n) ‘National Background Investigations Bureau’ (NBIB) means the Na-\ntional Background Investigations Bureau, established within the Office \nof Personnel Management under section 1103(a)(3) of title 5, United States \nCode, or a successor entity, with responsibility for conducting effective, \nefficient, and secure personnel background investigations pursuant to law, \nrule, regulation, or Executive Order.’’ \n(l) Redesignated section 1.3(o) of Executive Order 13467 is revised to \nread as follows: \n‘‘(o) ‘Sensitive Position’ means any position within or in support of a \ndepartment or agency, the occupant of which could bring about, by virtue \nof the nature of the position, a material adverse effect on the national \nsecurity, regardless of whether the occupant has access to classified infor-\nmation, and regardless of whether the occupant is an employee, a military \nservice member, or a contractor."},{"char_end":25955,"char_start":25056,"text":"The Executive Agents shall issue guidance to \nimplement this provision. \n‘‘(b) The aligned executive branch-wide vetting enterprise shall employ \nmodern and consistent standards and methods, enable innovations with \nenterprise information technology capabilities and end-to-end automation \nto the extent practicable, and ensure that relevant information maintained \nby agencies can be accessed and shared rapidly across the executive \nbranch, while protecting national security, protecting privacy-related infor-\nmation, protecting civil rights and civil liberties, ensuring resulting deci-\nsions are in the national interest and in accordance with due process \nrequirements, and providing the Federal Government with an effective \ntrusted workforce. \n‘‘(c) The investigative and adjudicative standards for fitness shall, to the \nextent practicable, be consistent with the standards for suitability."},{"char_end":40174,"char_start":33491,"text":"With respect to the \nSuitability Executive Agent functions, the Director: \n‘‘(i) shall, pursuant to sections 1103 and 1104 of title 5, United States \nCode, and the Civil Service Rules, be responsible for suitability and fitness \nby prescribing suitability standards and minimum standards of fitness \nfor employment; prescribing position designation requirements with regard \nto the risk to the efficiency and integrity of the service; prescribing applica-\nble investigative standards, policies, and procedures for suitability and \nfitness; prescribing suitability and fitness reciprocity standards; making \nsuitability determinations; and taking suitability actions; \n‘‘(ii) shall issue regulations, guidance, and standards to fulfill the Direc-\ntor’s responsibilities related to suitability and fitness under Executive Order \n13488 of January 16, 2009, as amended; \n‘‘(iii) shall promote reciprocal recognition of suitability or fitness deter-\nminations among the agencies, including acting as the final authority \nto arbitrate and resolve disputes among the agencies involving the reci-\nprocity of investigations and adjudications of suitability and fitness; \n‘‘(iv) shall continue to initially approve, and periodically review for \nrenewal, agencies’ requests to administer polygraphs in connection with \nappointment in the competitive service, in consultation with the Security \nExecutive Agent as appropriate; \n‘‘(v) shall make a continuing review of agency programs for suitability \nand fitness vetting to determine whether they are being implemented \naccording to this order; \n‘‘(vi) may issue guidelines and instructions to the heads of agencies \nto promote appropriate uniformity, centralization, efficiency, effectiveness, \nreciprocity, timeliness, and security in processes relating to determining \nsuitability or fitness; and \n‘‘(vii) shall, pursuant to section 1104 of title 5, United States Code, \nprescribe performance standards and a system of oversight for any suit-\nability or fitness function delegated by the Director to the head of another \nagency, including uniform and consistent policies and procedures to ensure \nthe effective, efficient, timely, and secure completion of delegated func-\ntions. \n‘‘(c) With respect to the Credentialing Executive Agent functions, the \nDirector of the Office of Personnel Management: \nVerDate Sep<11>2014 21:05 Jan 19, 2017 Jkt 241001 PO 00000 Frm 00011 Fmt 4705 Sfmt 4790 E:\\FR\\FM\\23JAE0.SGM 23JAE0asabaliauskas on DSK3SPTVN1PROD with E0\n=== PDF page 10 of 15 ===\n8124 Federal Register / Vol. 82, No. 13 / Monday, January 23, 2017 / Presidential Documents \n‘‘(i) shall develop standards for investigations, reinvestigations, and con-\ntinuous vetting for a covered individual’s eligibility for a personal identity \nverification credential permitting logical and physical access to federally \ncontrolled facilities and federally controlled information systems (PIV cre-\ndential); \n‘‘(ii) shall develop adjudicative guidelines for a covered individual’s \neligibility for a PIV credential; \n‘‘(iii) shall develop guidelines on reporting and recording determinations \nof eligibility for a PIV credential; \n‘‘(iv) shall develop standards for unfavorable determinations of National Background Investigations Bureau."},{"char_end":47559,"char_start":46801,"text":"The Secretary of Defense shall operate the data-\nbase in the information technology systems containing appropriate data \nrelevant to the granting, denial, or revocation of eligibility for access \nto classified information or eligibility for a sensitive position pertaining \nto military, civilian, or Government contractor personnel, see section \n3341(e) of title 50, United States Code, consistent with and following \nan explicit delegation from the Director of the Office of Personnel Manage-\nment pursuant to section 1104 of title 5, United States Code.’’ \n‘‘(c) Delegations and designations of investigative authority in place on \nthe date of establishment of the National Background Investigations Bureau \nshall remain in effect until amended or revoked."},{"char_end":50558,"char_start":48068,"text":"The Council shall hold the National Background \nVerDate Sep<11>2014 21:05 Jan 19, 2017 Jkt 241001 PO 00000 Frm 00014 Fmt 4705 Sfmt 4790 E:\\FR\\FM\\23JAE0.SGM 23JAE0asabaliauskas on DSK3SPTVN1PROD with E0\n=== PDF page 13 of 15 ===\n8127 Federal Register / Vol. 82, No. 13 / Monday, January 23, 2017 / Presidential Documents \nInvestigations Bureau accountable for the fulfillment of the responsibilities \nset forth in section 2.6(a) of this order.’’ \n(u) Subsections (b) and (c) of redesignated section 2.7 of Executive Order \n13467 are revised to read as follows: \n‘‘(b) Heads of agencies shall: \n‘‘(i) designate, or cause to be designated, as a ‘sensitive position,’ any \nposition occupied by a covered individual in which the occupant could \nbring about by virtue of the nature of the position, a material adverse \neffect on the national security; \n‘‘(ii) establish and maintain within their respective agencies, an effective \nprogram to ensure that employment and retention of any covered individual \nwithin the agency is clearly consistent with the interests of national security \nand, as applicable, meets standards for eligibility for access to classified \ninformation or to hold a sensitive position, suitability, fitness, or \ncredentialing, established by the respective Executive Agent; \n‘‘(iii) carry out any function assigned to the agency head by the Chair, \nand shall assist the Chair, the Council, the Executive Agents, the National \nBackground Investigations Bureau, and the Department of Defense in car-\nrying out any function under sections 2.4, 2.5, and 2.6 of this order; \n‘‘(iv) implement any policy or procedure established pursuant to this \norder; \n‘‘(v) to the extent permitted by law, make available to the Council, \nthe Executive Agents, the National Background Investigations Bureau, and \nthe Department of Defense such information as may be requested to imple-\nment this order, including information necessary to implement enterprise- \nwide vetting policies and procedures; \n‘‘(vi) except as authorized by section 3341(e)(5) of title 50, United States \nCode, promptly furnish, or cause to be promptly furnished, to the Office \nof Personnel Management the information deemed by the Executive Agents \nto be necessary for purposes of record keeping and reciprocity including, \nbut not limited to, the date on which a background investigation is initiated, \nthe date on which the background investigation is closed, and the specific \nadjudicative or access decision made."},{"char_end":57363,"char_start":56093,"text":"VerDate Sep<11>2014 21:05 Jan 19, 2017 Jkt 241001 PO 00000 Frm 00016 Fmt 4705 Sfmt 4790 E:\\FR\\FM\\23JAE0.SGM 23JAE0asabaliauskas on DSK3SPTVN1PROD with E0\n=== PDF page 15 of 15 ===\n8129 Federal Register / Vol. 82, No. 13 / Monday, January 23, 2017 / Presidential Documents \n‘‘(f) Existing delegations of authority made pursuant to Executive Order \n13381 of June 27, 2005, as amended, to any agency relating to granting \neligibility for access to classified information shall remain in effect, subject \nto the exercise of authorities pursuant to this order to revise or revoke \nsuch delegation. \n‘‘(g) Existing delegations of authority made by the Office of Personnel \nManagement to any agency relating to suitability or fitness shall remain \nin effect, subject to the exercise of authorities to revise or revoke such \ndelegations. \n‘‘(h) If any provision of this order or the application of such provision \nis held to be invalid, the remainder of this order shall not be affected. \n‘‘(i) This order is not intended to, and does not, create any right or \nbenefit, substantive or procedural, enforceable at law or in equity by \nany party against the United States, its departments, agencies, or entities, \nits officers, employees, or agents, or any other person.’’ \nSec. 4."}],"exceptions_text":[],"filing_date":null,"id":"ACT:EO:12333>EO:13764@c382ec9849dedfc0","names_target":true,"notes":"Machine lead only; no legal ending or Effective wording is ambiguous, section-specific, or has no determinable date.","provision_label":"Sec. 3.","reaches_target_via":"","savings_phrases":[],"scope":"partial","signing_date":"2017-01-17","target_id":"EO:12333","verb":"amend"}
  Text: [T3122f33be1dbeac056521717](#t3122f33be1dbeac056521717); absolute characters 53395–54089
- **ACT:EO:12333>EO:14086**; S5257dc00c476e5bb2937a020; {"actor_id":"EO:14086","char_end":50792,"char_start":49053,"confidence":"medium","effective_class":"on_signing","effective_date":"2022-10-07","effective_wording":[{"char_end":8938,"char_start":8629,"text":"(A) Under section 102A of the National Security Act of 1947, as amended \n(50 U.S.C. 3024), the Director must establish priorities for the Intelligence \nCommunity to ensure the timely and effective collection of national intel-\nligence, including national intelligence collected through signals intel-\nligence."},{"char_end":46232,"char_start":44545,"text":"(i) To implement the redress mechanism established by section 3 of this \norder, the Attorney General is authorized to designate a country or regional \neconomic integration organization as a qualifying state for purposes of \nthe redress mechanism established pursuant to section 3 of this order, \neffective immediately or on a date specified by the Attorney General, \nif the Attorney General determines, in consultation with the Secretary \nof State, the Secretary of Commerce, and the Director, that: \n(A) the laws of the country, the regional economic integration organiza-\ntion, or the regional economic integration organization’s member countries \nrequire appropriate safeguards in the conduct of signals intelligence activi-\nties for United States persons’ personal information that is transferred \nfrom the United States to the territory of the country or a member country \nof the regional economic integration organization; \nVerDate Sep<11>2014 16:13 Oct 13, 2022 Jkt 259001 PO 00000 Frm 00011 Fmt 4705 Sfmt 4790 E:\\FR\\FM\\14OCE0.SGM 14OCE0jspears on DSK121TN23PROD with PREZ DOCS 3\n=== PDF page 12 of 15 ===\n62294 Federal Register / Vol. 87, No. 198 / Friday, October 14, 2022 / Presidential Documents \n(B) the country, the regional economic integration organization, or the \nregional economic integration organization’s member countries of the re-\ngional economic integration organization permit, or are anticipated to per-\nmit, the transfer of personal information for commercial purposes between \nthe territory of that country or those member countries and the territory \nof the United States; and \n(C) such designation would advance the national interests of the United \nStates."},{"char_end":47330,"char_start":46234,"text":"(ii) The Attorney General may revoke or amend such a designation, effective \nimmediately or on a date specified by the Attorney General, if the Attorney \nGeneral determines, in consultation with the Secretary of State, the Sec-\nretary of Commerce, and the Director, that: \n(A) the country, the regional economic integration organization, or the \nregional economic integration organization’s member countries do not pro-\nvide appropriate safeguards in the conduct of signals intelligence activities \nfor United States persons’ personal information that is transferred from \nthe United States to the territory of the country or to a member country \nof the regional economic integration organization; \n(B) the country, the regional economic integration organization, or the \nregional economic integration organization’s member countries do not per-\nmit the transfer of personal information for commercial purposes between \nthe territory of that country or those member countries and the territory \nof the United States; or \n(C) such designation is not in the national interests of the United States."},{"char_end":50792,"char_start":49053,"text":"(d) ‘‘Covered violation’’ means a violation that: \n(i) arises from signals intelligence activities conducted after the date of \nthis order regarding data transferred to the United States from a qualifying \nstate after the effective date of the Attorney General’s designation for \nsuch state, as provided in section 3(f)(i) of this order; \n(ii) adversely affects the complainant’s individual privacy and civil liberties \ninterests; and \n(iii) violates one or more of the following: \n(A) the United States Constitution; \nVerDate Sep<11>2014 16:13 Oct 13, 2022 Jkt 259001 PO 00000 Frm 00012 Fmt 4705 Sfmt 4790 E:\\FR\\FM\\14OCE0.SGM 14OCE0jspears on DSK121TN23PROD with PREZ DOCS 3\n=== PDF page 13 of 15 ===\n62295 Federal Register / Vol. 87, No. 198 / Friday, October 14, 2022 / Presidential Documents \n(B) the applicable sections of FISA or any applicable FISC-approved \nprocedures; \n(C) Executive Order 12333 or any applicable agency procedures pursuant \nto Executive Order 12333; \n(D) this order or any applicable agency policies and procedures issued \nor updated pursuant to this order (or the policies and procedures identified \nin section 2(c)(iv)(A) of this order before they are updated pursuant to \nsection 2(c)(iv)(B) of this order); \n(E) any successor statute, order, policies, or procedures to those identified \nin section 4(d)(iii)(B)–(D) of this order; or \n(F) any other statute, order, policies, or procedures adopted after the \ndate of this order that provides privacy and civil liberties safeguards \nwith respect to United States signals intelligence activities within the \nscope of this order, as identified in a list published and updated by \nthe Attorney General, in consultation with the Director of National Intel-\nligence."},{"char_end":53477,"char_start":51870,"text":"(k) ‘‘Qualifying complaint’’ means a complaint, submitted in writing, that: \n(i) alleges a covered violation has occurred that pertains to personal infor-\nmation of or about the complainant, a natural person, reasonably believed \nto have been transferred to the United States from a qualifying state \nafter the effective date of the Attorney General’s designation for such \nstate, as provided in section 3(f)(i) of this order; \n(ii) includes the following basic information to enable a review: information \nthat forms the basis for alleging that a covered violation has occurred, \nwhich need not demonstrate that the complainant’s data has in fact been \nsubject to United States signals intelligence activities; the nature of the \nrelief sought; the specific means by which personal information of or \nabout the complainant was believed to have been transmitted to the United \nStates; the identities of the United States Government entities believed \nto be involved in the alleged violation (if known); and any other measures \nthe complainant pursued to obtain the relief requested and the response \nreceived through those other measures; \n(iii) is not frivolous, vexatious, or made in bad faith; \n(iv) is brought on behalf of the complainant, acting on that person’s \nown behalf, and not as a representative of a governmental, nongovern-\nmental, or intergovernmental organization; and \n(v) is transmitted by the appropriate public authority in a qualifying \nstate, after it has verified the identity of the complainant and that the \ncomplaint satisfies the conditions of section 5(k)(i)–(iv) of this order."}],"exceptions_text":[],"filing_date":null,"id":"ACT:EO:12333>EO:14086","names_target":true,"notes":"Machine lead only; no legal ending or revival asserted. Express signing-date wording; supplied signing date still needs source confirmation.","provision_label":"Sec. 4.","reaches_target_via":"","savings_phrases":["(e) Savings clause."],"scope":"partial","signing_date":"2022-10-07","target_id":"EO:12333","verb":"transfer"}

- **ACT:EO:12333>EO:14086@ec1b30f3050b5bd4**; S5257dc00c476e5bb2937a020; {"actor_id":"EO:14086","char_end":50792,"char_start":49053,"confidence":"medium","effective_class":"on_signing","effective_date":"2022-10-07","effective_wording":[{"char_end":8938,"char_start":8629,"text":"(A) Under section 102A of the National Security Act of 1947, as amended \n(50 U.S.C. 3024), the Director must establish priorities for the Intelligence \nCommunity to ensure the timely and effective collection of national intel-\nligence, including national intelligence collected through signals intel-\nligence."},{"char_end":46232,"char_start":44545,"text":"(i) To implement the redress mechanism established by section 3 of this \norder, the Attorney General is authorized to designate a country or regional \neconomic integration organization as a qualifying state for purposes of \nthe redress mechanism established pursuant to section 3 of this order, \neffective immediately or on a date specified by the Attorney General, \nif the Attorney General determines, in consultation with the Secretary \nof State, the Secretary of Commerce, and the Director, that: \n(A) the laws of the country, the regional economic integration organiza-\ntion, or the regional economic integration organization’s member countries \nrequire appropriate safeguards in the conduct of signals intelligence activi-\nties for United States persons’ personal information that is transferred \nfrom the United States to the territory of the country or a member country \nof the regional economic integration organization; \nVerDate Sep<11>2014 16:13 Oct 13, 2022 Jkt 259001 PO 00000 Frm 00011 Fmt 4705 Sfmt 4790 E:\\FR\\FM\\14OCE0.SGM 14OCE0jspears on DSK121TN23PROD with PREZ DOCS 3\n=== PDF page 12 of 15 ===\n62294 Federal Register / Vol. 87, No. 198 / Friday, October 14, 2022 / Presidential Documents \n(B) the country, the regional economic integration organization, or the \nregional economic integration organization’s member countries of the re-\ngional economic integration organization permit, or are anticipated to per-\nmit, the transfer of personal information for commercial purposes between \nthe territory of that country or those member countries and the territory \nof the United States; and \n(C) such designation would advance the national interests of the United \nStates."},{"char_end":47330,"char_start":46234,"text":"(ii) The Attorney General may revoke or amend such a designation, effective \nimmediately or on a date specified by the Attorney General, if the Attorney \nGeneral determines, in consultation with the Secretary of State, the Sec-\nretary of Commerce, and the Director, that: \n(A) the country, the regional economic integration organization, or the \nregional economic integration organization’s member countries do not pro-\nvide appropriate safeguards in the conduct of signals intelligence activities \nfor United States persons’ personal information that is transferred from \nthe United States to the territory of the country or to a member country \nof the regional economic integration organization; \n(B) the country, the regional economic integration organization, or the \nregional economic integration organization’s member countries do not per-\nmit the transfer of personal information for commercial purposes between \nthe territory of that country or those member countries and the territory \nof the United States; or \n(C) such designation is not in the national interests of the United States."},{"char_end":50792,"char_start":49053,"text":"(d) ‘‘Covered violation’’ means a violation that: \n(i) arises from signals intelligence activities conducted after the date of \nthis order regarding data transferred to the United States from a qualifying \nstate after the effective date of the Attorney General’s designation for \nsuch state, as provided in section 3(f)(i) of this order; \n(ii) adversely affects the complainant’s individual privacy and civil liberties \ninterests; and \n(iii) violates one or more of the following: \n(A) the United States Constitution; \nVerDate Sep<11>2014 16:13 Oct 13, 2022 Jkt 259001 PO 00000 Frm 00012 Fmt 4705 Sfmt 4790 E:\\FR\\FM\\14OCE0.SGM 14OCE0jspears on DSK121TN23PROD with PREZ DOCS 3\n=== PDF page 13 of 15 ===\n62295 Federal Register / Vol. 87, No. 198 / Friday, October 14, 2022 / Presidential Documents \n(B) the applicable sections of FISA or any applicable FISC-approved \nprocedures; \n(C) Executive Order 12333 or any applicable agency procedures pursuant \nto Executive Order 12333; \n(D) this order or any applicable agency policies and procedures issued \nor updated pursuant to this order (or the policies and procedures identified \nin section 2(c)(iv)(A) of this order before they are updated pursuant to \nsection 2(c)(iv)(B) of this order); \n(E) any successor statute, order, policies, or procedures to those identified \nin section 4(d)(iii)(B)–(D) of this order; or \n(F) any other statute, order, policies, or procedures adopted after the \ndate of this order that provides privacy and civil liberties safeguards \nwith respect to United States signals intelligence activities within the \nscope of this order, as identified in a list published and updated by \nthe Attorney General, in consultation with the Director of National Intel-\nligence."},{"char_end":53477,"char_start":51870,"text":"(k) ‘‘Qualifying complaint’’ means a complaint, submitted in writing, that: \n(i) alleges a covered violation has occurred that pertains to personal infor-\nmation of or about the complainant, a natural person, reasonably believed \nto have been transferred to the United States from a qualifying state \nafter the effective date of the Attorney General’s designation for such \nstate, as provided in section 3(f)(i) of this order; \n(ii) includes the following basic information to enable a review: information \nthat forms the basis for alleging that a covered violation has occurred, \nwhich need not demonstrate that the complainant’s data has in fact been \nsubject to United States signals intelligence activities; the nature of the \nrelief sought; the specific means by which personal information of or \nabout the complainant was believed to have been transmitted to the United \nStates; the identities of the United States Government entities believed \nto be involved in the alleged violation (if known); and any other measures \nthe complainant pursued to obtain the relief requested and the response \nreceived through those other measures; \n(iii) is not frivolous, vexatious, or made in bad faith; \n(iv) is brought on behalf of the complainant, acting on that person’s \nown behalf, and not as a representative of a governmental, nongovern-\nmental, or intergovernmental organization; and \n(v) is transmitted by the appropriate public authority in a qualifying \nstate, after it has verified the identity of the complainant and that the \ncomplaint satisfies the conditions of section 5(k)(i)–(iv) of this order."}],"exceptions_text":[],"filing_date":null,"id":"ACT:EO:12333>EO:14086@ec1b30f3050b5bd4","names_target":true,"notes":"Machine lead only; no legal ending or revival asserted. chronology does not decide legal effect.","provision_text":"Executive Order 12333 \nof December 4, 1981, as amended, is further amended as follows: \n(a) Subsection 1.5(a) is amended to read:\n‘‘(a)(1) Act as the principal adviser to the President for intelligence \nmatters related to the national security;\n‘‘(2) Act as the principal adviser to the National Security Council \nand Homeland Security Council for intelligence matters related to the \nnational security; and \n(b) Subsection 1.5(b) is amended to read:\n‘‘(b)(1) Develop such objectives and guidance for the Intelligence Commu-\nnity necessary, in the Director’s judgment, to ensure timely and effective \ncollection, processing, analysis, and dissemination of intelligence, of what-\never nature and from whatever source derived, concerning current and \npotential threats to the security of the United States and its interests, \nand to ensure that the National Foreign Intelligence Program (NFIP) is \nstructured adequately to achieve these requirements; and\n‘‘(2) Working with the Intelligence Community, ensure that United States \nintelligence collection activities are integrated in: (i) collecting against \nenduring and emerging national security intelligence issues; (ii) maximizing \nthe value to the national security; and (iii) ensuring that all collected \ndata is available to the maximum extent practicable for integration, anal-\nysis, and dissemination to those who can act on, add value to, or otherwise \napply it to mission needs.’’\n(c) Subsection 1.5(g) is amended to read:\n‘‘(g)(1) Establish common security and access standards for managing \nand handling intelligence systems, information, and products, with special \nemphasis on facilitating:\n‘‘(A) the fullest and most prompt sharing of information practicable, \nassigning the highest priority to detecting, preventing, preempting, and \ndisrupting terrorist threats against our homeland, our people, our allies, \nand our interests; and\n‘‘(B) the establishment of interface standards for an interoperable informa-\ntion sharing enterprise that facilitates the automated sharing of intelligence \ninformation among agencies within the Intelligence Community.","sections_touched":["Subsection 1","Subsection 1","Subsection 1"],"signing_date":"2004-08-27","source":{"acceptable_as_original":false,"filing_date":null,"grade":"held_text_lead","instrument_id":"EO:13355","page_or_item":"69 FR 53593, PDF pages 1-5","requires_page_check":false,"sha256":"dd9f3555882d2660732d5097285d97db13f57c4b17b801a29bc734ad3c71d474","signing_date":"2004-08-27","text_path":"jobs/clause-drafts/output/texts/cd-job-fr-originals-13355-dd9f355588.txt","text_sha256":"3055ec2869ea20747105a1d149bf5680829d31395ea4933587985d4e2ee7265c","url":"https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2004-09-01/pdf/04-20051.pdf"},"verb":"amend"},{"actor_id":"EO:13355","char_end":3752,"char_start":1637,"confidence":"medium","how_named":"direct","id":"CHAIN:EO:12333#11","notes":"Change wording lead; chronology does not decide legal effect.","provision_text":"Executive Order 12829, as \namended, is hereby further amended as follows: \n(a) the second paragraph is amended by inserting ‘‘the Intelligence Reform \nand Terrorism Prevention Act of 2004,’’ after ‘‘the National Security Act \nof 1947, as amended,’’; \n(b) Sec. 101(b) is amended to read as follows: ‘‘The National Industrial \nSecurity Program shall provide for the protection of information classified \npursuant to Executive Order 13526 of December 29, 2009, or any predecessor \nor successor order, and the Atomic Energy Act of 1954, as amended (42 \nU.S.C. 2011 et seq.).’’; \n(c) Sec. 102(b) is amended by replacing the first paragraph with: ‘‘In \nconsultation with the National Security Advisor, the Director of the Informa-\ntion Security Oversight Office, in accordance with Executive Order 13526 \nof December 29, 2009, shall be responsible for implementing and monitoring \nthe National Industrial Security Program and shall:’’; chronology does not decide legal effect.","provision_text":"(v) Section 3 of Executive Order 13467 is revised to read as follows:\n\n\"Sec. 3. General Provisions. (a) Executive Order 13381 of June 27, 2005, as amended, and Executive Order 10450 of April 27, 1953, as amended, are revoked. By revoking Executive Order 10450 of April 27, 1953, as amended, there is no intent to alter the requirement for an investigation for national security purposes or the \"clearly consistent with the interest of national security\" standard prescribed by that Executive Order for making the determinations referenced in section 2.7(b)(ii). Further, suitability, fitness, credentialing, and national security eligibility regulations, standards and guidance issued by, or interagency agreements entered into by, the Council, the Executive Agents, or any agency pursuant to Executive Order 10450 of\n\nApril 27, 1953, as amended, shall remain valid until superseded. Nothing in this order shall:\n\n\"(i) supersede, impede, or otherwise affect:\n\n\"(A) Executive Order 10577 of November 23, 1954, as amended;\n\n\"(B) Executive Order 12333 of December 4, 1981, as amended;\n\n\"(C) Executive Order 12829 of January 6, 1993, as amended; or\n\n\"(D) Executive Order 13526 of December 29, 2009; or\n\n\"(ii) diminish or otherwise affect the denial and revocation procedures provided to individuals covered by Executive Order 10865 of February 20, 1960, as amended; or\n\n\"(iii) be applied in such a way as to affect any administrative proceeding pending on the date of this order.\n\n\"(b) Executive Order 12968 of August 2, 1995, is amended:\n\n\"(i) by inserting: 'Sec. 3.5. Continuous Evaluation. An individual who has been determined to be eligible for or who currently has access to classified information shall be subject to continuous evaluation as further defined by and under standards (including, but not limited to, the frequency of such evaluation) as determined by the Director of National Intelligence.'; and\n\n\"(ii) by striking 'the Security Policy Board shall make recommendations to the President through the Assistant to the President for National Security Affairs' in section 6.3(a) and inserting in lieu thereof 'the Director of National Intelligence shall serve as the final authority';\n\n\"(iii) by striking 'Security Policy Board' and inserting in lieu thereof 'Security Executive Agent' in each instance;\n\n\"(iv) by striking 'the Board' in section 1.1(j) and inserting in lieu thereof 'the Security Executive Agent'; and\n\n\"(v) by inserting 'or appropriate automated procedures' in section 3.1(b) after 'by appropriately trained adjudicative personnel'.\n\n\"(c) Provisions of Executive Order 12968 of August 2, 1995, as amended, that apply to eligibility for access to classified information shall apply to eligibility to hold any sensitive position regardless of whether that sensitive position requires access to classified information, subject to the Security Executive Agent issuing implementing or clarifying guidance regarding requirements for sensitive positions. Nothing in this order shall supersede, impede, or otherwise affect the remainder of Executive Order 12968 of August 2, 1995, as amended.\n\n\"(d) Nothing in this order shall be construed to impair or otherwise affect the:\n\n\"(i) authority granted by law to a department or agency, or the head thereof; or\n\n\"(ii) functions of the Director of the Office of Management and Budget relating to budgetary, administrative, or legislative proposals.\n\n\"(e) This order shall be implemented consistent with applicable law and subject to the availability of appropriations.\n\n\"(f) Existing delegations of authority made pursuant to Executive Order 13381 of June 27, 2005, as amended, to any agency relating to granting eligibility for access to classified information shall remain in effect, subject to the exercise of authorities pursuant to this order to revise or revoke such delegation.\n\n\"(g) Existing delegations of authority made by the Office of Personnel Management to any agency relating to suitability or fitness shall remain in effect, subject to the exercise of authorities to revise or revoke such delegations.\n\n\"(h) If any provision of this order or the application of such provision is held to be invalid, the remainder of this order shall not be affected.\n\n\"(i) This order is not intended to, and does not, create any right or benefit, substantive or procedural, enforceable at law or in equity by any party against the United States, its departments, agencies, or entities, its officers, employees, or agents, or any other person.\"","sections_touched":["Section 3","section 2","section 6","section 1","section 3"],"signing_date":"2017-01-17","source":{"acceptable_as_original":false,"archival_id":"app:node/218590","filing_date":null,"grade":"mirror_transcription","instrument_id":"EO:13764","location_confidence":"medium","location_verified":false,"page_or_item":"Executive Order 13764—Amending the Civil Service Rules, Executive Order 13488, and Executive Order 13467 To Modernize the Executive Branch-Wide Governance Structure and Processes for Security Clearances, Suitability and Fitness for Employment, and Credentialing, and Related Matters; ## Valla review leads and component attestations

Review lead only. Every case needs separate applicability, earlier-ending, scope, independent-command, savings and independent whole-case review.
Preparation attestations never approve legal conclusions or replace whole-case review.
